How depth collapses when the trail is longer than the space

rules.statement: The trail shows the object's place in the product hierarchy, never the reader's click history; a trail that changes when you arrive from search is a lie about structure.
Long trails keep the first and last two levels and collapse the middle into one expansion, which opens as a menu rather than truncating with an ellipsis.
The current page is plain text with aria-current='page'; it is not a link to itself, and the separators are hidden from assistive technology.
On small screens the trail collapses to the parent plus the current page; it never turns into a bare back arrow that hides where the reader is.
Two levels or fewer is not a breadcrumb; the page title and the sidebar already say it.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: no async data in the trail; the collapsed expansion loads its ancestors once and caches them for the page's lifetime

motion.reducedMotion: the menu appears instantly in place

transitions.trigger: ancestors are fetched for the expansion

motion.motion: a pending row appears in the menu over 120ms
a retry row replaces the pending row over 120ms
the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.motion: the control returns to pending over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the control returns to pending instantly

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Tell a reader where the page sits in the product, and give them one click back up the hierarchy.
useCases: see that a record belongs to a project inside a workspace
return to a parent collection after a deep link
nicheDifferences: Operate products are deep, and deep links are how people arrive
A trail is the only orientation cue that survives a direct link
inputs: the hierarchy depth and its stable names
whether the trail must be linkable at every level
anatomy: a collapse control for the middle
the current page as text with aria-current
styling: single line, 14 px, muted ancestors and a stronger current page
separators are slashes drawn in CSS, hidden from screen readers
no hover underline on the current page because it is not a link
a11y: wrapped in nav with aria-label='Breadcrumb' and an ordered list
the collapse control is a button with an expanded state
responsive: collapses to parent plus current under 640 px
labels truncate only in the middle levels, never the current page
the trail never wraps to three lines; it collapses instead
copy: level names match the sidebar's names exactly
the collapse control says how many levels it hides
no 'Home > ... > Page' filler when the reader is already home
alternatives: a back link when the hierarchy is only one level deep
an in-page section list when the depth is within one document
the sidebar alone when the tree is always visible
acceptance: the trail reflects hierarchy, not click history
the current page is text with aria-current and is not self-linked
a long trail collapses the middle into an expansion menu
at 320 px the trail is parent plus current
two levels or fewer renders no breadcrumb at all
failureCases: the trail changes depending on how the reader arrived
the current page links to itself
the ellipsis is a dead end with no menu
the mobile version becomes a back arrow that hides the hierarchy
